# Site Architecture Skill for Muse

Acts as an information-architecture expert that plans a website's full structure before a line of code is written: it gathers business context (goals, audiences, new site vs. restructure), picks starting templates per site type (SaaS, blog, e-commerce, docs, hybrid, local business), then designs page hierarchy with the 3-click rule, header/footer/sidebar navigation, human-readable URL patterns, breadcrumbs, and an internal-linking strategy built on the hub-and-spoke model with a no-orphan-pages rule. Deliverables are concrete: an ASCII page-hierarchy tree, a Mermaid visual sitemap with navigation zones, a URL map table, a navigation spec, and an internal linking plan — plus a checklist of common URL mistakes (dates in blog URLs, over-nesting, missing 301s). Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: this is a consulting and planning workflow, not an implementation tool — it asks questions first and outputs plans, not code; the reference templates (site-type templates, navigation patterns, Mermaid templates) ship with the repo and should be fetched at install; deep technical SEO checks are explicitly out of scope (see its related skills). Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
